newsitem.title: JAPAN: N. Korea says U.S. sanctions hamper peace talks.
newsitem.headline: N. Korea says U.S. sanctions hamper peace talks.

text.p: North Korea on Friday accused the United States of using economic sanctions against Pyongyang as a means to turn the ongoing peace talks to its advantage.
"The U.S. intends to secure concessions from the DPRK (North Korea) by means of sanction and turn the "quad talks" favourable to it," the official newspaper Rodong Sinmun said in its commentary.
"The U.S. position concerning the economic sanctions is a wanton violation of the DPRK-U.S. framework agreement," the newspaper said.
"We cannot sit on the fence now that the U.S. has unhesitatingly violated the agreement and abused "four-way talks" as means of pressure," it said.
The commentary was carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo.

Diplomats from the United States, China, North Korea and South Korea met this week in New York for preliminary talks aimed at replacing the fraying Korean War armistice with a more durable peace on the bitterly divided Korean peninsula.
The four parties failed on Thursday to agree on the agenda of the talks, with North Korea demanding that the withdrawal of U.S. troops in South Korea be included on the agenda.
But they said they would resume their sessions on September 15 to continue working on the logistics of negotiations.
